You are editing a single HTML file to create a WhatsApp variant of an existing Telegram-based onboarding app. Work ONLY on this file: /workspace/agent/tmp_shellano_hotfix/whatsapp.html This is a copy of the live "Click2Agent" onboarding app (index.html, ~1159 lines). It is a bilingual (Hebrew `he` + English `en`) slide app. Copy lives in a JS object `const S = { he:{...}, en:{...} }` (Hebrew starts ~line 519, English is the mirror block after it). Screens are `
` blocks using `data-i18n` / `data-i18n-html` / `data-i18n-ph` keys that map into S. There is also a JS block near the bottom handling form submit + handoff (search for `api/register`, `deepLink`, `FALLBACK`, `provision`). GOAL: swap the whole flow from Telegram to WhatsApp. The sender's WhatsApp phone number IS their identity — no deep-link codes, no app install needed. Make ALL of these changes in BOTH `he` and `en`, keeping tone/voice identical to the original (warm, confident, Elia Ben Cnaan's first-person voice). Never use em-dashes. Keep Hebrew RTL correct. REQUIRED CHANGES: 1. SECURITY CARD #2 (keys `sec2T` / `sec2B`, appears both in the `
` markup ~line 416 AND in S.he/S.en). Currently "טלגרם, ערוץ פרטי ומוצפן" / about Telegram. Change to WhatsApp: - he sec2T: "וואטסאפ, ערוץ שכבר יש לך" sec2B: "כל השיחה עוברת בוואטסאפ, מוצפנת מקצה לקצה, ונפרדת מהמייל, מהדרייב ומכל מערכת אחרת." - en sec2T: "WhatsApp, a channel you already have" sec2B: "Every conversation runs over WhatsApp, end-to-end encrypted, separate from your email, drive and every other system." 2. FORM SCREEN lead (`formLead`, in markup ~line 444 and in S). Currently about working from inside Telegram. Rewrite for WhatsApp, e.g.: - he: "הסוכן שלך עובד מתוך וואטסאפ, ומשם תתנהל כל העבודה איתו. המספר שממנו תכתוב הופך לזהות שלך, בלי קודים ובלי התקנות. עוד כמה פרטים, והוא כבר מתחיל." - en: "Your agent works right inside WhatsApp, and everything runs from there. The number you message from becomes your identity, with no codes and nothing to install. A few more details and it gets started." 3. DOWNLOAD ROW: remove the Telegram download prompt + buttons entirely. In the markup that's the `

` (~line 445) and the `

...
` (~lines 446-455). DELETE both those elements. Replace them with a single small note element styled like a subtle hint (reuse the existing `dl-prompt` class is fine) with text: - he: "צריך שיהיה לך וואטסאפ, ולכולם כבר יש, אז אין מה להתקין." - en: "You just need WhatsApp, and everyone already has it, so there is nothing to install." Do this via a data-i18n key `waNote` (add `waNote` to both S.he and S.en with the strings above), and put `

` where the download row was. Remove the now-unused keys `dlPrompt`, `dlMobile`, `dlDesktop` from S (optional but clean). 4. SINGLE CHECKBOX: currently there are TWO consent checkboxes in the form (~lines 479-486): `#tgConsentWrap` ("הורדתי טלגרם, אפשר להתחיל") and `#consentWrap` (privacy policy). DELETE the entire `tgConsentWrap` label block (the Telegram-download checkbox). Keep ONLY the privacy/terms checkbox. Then check the JS validation: find where `inTgConsent` is referenced (form validation / whether the CTA is enabled) and remove that requirement so the form is valid with just name/email/phone + the single privacy checkbox. Remove the `tgConsent` key from S. 5. PRIVACY/CONSENT TEXT: update the consent label + any privacy policy copy to cover WhatsApp. The `consent` key (S.he/S.en, ~line 554) currently: "קראתי ואישרתי את מדיניות הפרטיות ותנאי השימוש". Keep the link structure but ensure the linked policy content (search the file for a privacy/policy modal or sheet — look for "מדיניות" / "privacy" / policy text blocks) mentions WhatsApp instead of Telegram where relevant (e.g. "the WhatsApp number you message from is your identity", conversations run over WhatsApp). If there is no separate policy modal, just ensure the consent line itself is coherent for WhatsApp. 6. HANDOFF / SUBMIT JS: currently on submit the app POSTs to `https://nanohubdemo.vercel.app/api/register` and redirects to a returned Telegram `deepLink` (with a `FALLBACK` t.me/telegram.me link). Replace this so submit instead opens WhatsApp with a prefilled first message to the dedicated number, carrying the user's name + source. Use number `972548284911`. Build the link like: ``` var nm = (firstName + ' ' + lastName).trim(); // use whatever the form's name vars are var msg = (LANG==='he') ? ('היי, קוראים לי ' + nm + ', אשמח לפתוח סוכן אישי.') : ('Hi, my name is ' + nm + ". I'd like to open my personal agent."); if (SRC) msg += ' (' + SRC + ')'; // SRC = existing source/utm value if the file already computes one; if a src is read from the URL query, reuse it, else omit var waUrl = 'https://wa.me/972548284911?text=' + encodeURIComponent(msg); window.location.href = waUrl; ``` Preserve any existing analytics call (e.g. `window.__trk` / `register_submit` tracking) — keep the tracking line, just change the destination from the fetch/deepLink to the wa.me redirect. Remove the now-dead fetch/provision/FALLBACK code path for the deep link. Look at how the file currently reads first/last name and any `src` query param and reuse those exact variables. 7. META / SEO description tags (lines ~13, 17, 26) and `docTitle` in S: change "ישר בטלגרם" / "inside Telegram" to WhatsApp equivalents ("ישר בוואטסאפ" / "inside WhatsApp"). 8. TRUST / HERO lines: `trust` (he ~line 524: "חינם להתנסות · קליק אחד מהנייד · מאובטח לחלוטין") is fine as is. Check `heroLead` and any other visible copy for the word "טלגרם"/"Telegram" and swap to WhatsApp. Do a final search for "טלגרם" and "Telegram" across the whole file (excluding CSS class names / color variables like `--tg-bg`, `.tg-`, and the chat-bubble demo styling which is cosmetic) and swap every USER-VISIBLE occurrence to WhatsApp. Leave CSS variable names and class names untouched (renaming them risks breaking styles). DO NOT: - Do not touch index.html, c2a.html, shellano.html, or any other file. - Do not rename CSS classes/variables. - Do not deploy (I will deploy). - Do not add em-dashes. VERIFY before finishing: - `grep -n 'טלגרם\|Telegram' whatsapp.html` returns only CSS/class/comment lines, no user-visible copy. - The form has exactly ONE checkbox (privacy) and no Telegram-download checkbox. - The download button row is gone, replaced by the single waNote line. - Submit builds a wa.me/972548284911 URL with the prefilled name message. - Both he and en blocks are updated symmetrically. - No `undefined` i18n keys: any data-i18n key used in markup exists in both S.he and S.en, and you didn't leave references to deleted keys (dlPrompt/dlMobile/dlDesktop/tgConsent) in the markup. When done, report a concise summary of exactly what you changed (by key/line), and the result of the two verification greps.

- agent-browser: Browse the web for any task — research topics, read articles, interact with web apps, fill forms, take screenshots, extract data, and test web pages. Use whenever a browser would be useful, not just when the user explicitly asks.
- frontend-engineer: Pro frontend engineering discipline. Enforces build-test-verify workflow for every web project. Never declare done until the site is built, tested, responsive, accessible, and visually verified in a real browser. Use alongside vercel-cli for production-quality deployments.
- onecli-gateway: OneCLI Gateway: transparent HTTPS proxy that injects stored credentials into outbound calls. You MUST use this skill when the user asks you to read emails, check calendar, access GitHub repos, create issues, check Stripe payments, or interact with ANY external service or API. Do NOT use browser extensions or OAuth CLI tools. Make HTTP requests directly; the gateway injects credentials automatically.
- self-customize: Customize your own agent — add capabilities, install packages, add MCP servers, edit code or CLAUDE.md. Use when the user asks you to add a feature, install a tool, or modify how you work. For non-trivial code changes, delegate to a builder agent via create_agent.
- slack-formatting: Format messages for Slack using mrkdwn syntax. Use when responding to Slack channels (folder starts with "slack_" or JID contains slack identifiers).
- vercel-cli: Deploy apps to Vercel. Use when asked to deploy, ship, or publish a web application, or manage Vercel projects, domains, and environment variables.
- welcome: Introduce yourself to a newly connected channel. Triggered automatically when a channel is first wired. Send a friendly greeting and brief overview of what you can do.
- whatsapp-formatting: Format messages for WhatsApp, including mentions that render as real WhatsApp tags. Use when responding in a WhatsApp conversation (platform_id / chatJid ends with @s.whatsapp.net or @g.us).
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
